trust_decision.summary: Request-body bytes queued by the ASGI receive handler are application data and must never be written to process stdout; the trust boundary is Body.__await__, which accumulates the queued chunks and must return them without emitting them.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the stray debug print in Body.__await__ explicitly, so a reader of the summary goes straight to this line.

fix_sites.entry_point: Request.get_data() and the public accessors built on it (request.data, request.get_json/request.json, request.form and request.values for url-encoded bodies, app.test_request_context)
POST /echo in the bundled example app
fix_sites.module_kind: example application handler (not part of the distributed library)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The second source change is in examples/api, an unshipped demo app that prints only is_json/mimetype (not the body), so a solver can argue it is not part of the library's flaw and leave it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same accumulation loop enforces MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH on chunked bodies and caches the result in _data; rewriting it as 'return await self.get()' or deleting the loop drops the size limit and the cached-body contract.

O6_input_shapes: multi-chunk bodies: the print runs once per dequeued chunk and re-emits the cumulative bytearray (src/quart/wrappers/request.py:100-102)
whole-body reads: request.data and request.get_data() await the body directly (src/quart/wrappers/request.py:253-254, 288-289)
JSON bodies: get_json -> get_data -> await body (src/quart/wrappers/request.py:387-390)
url-encoded form posts: the parser does '(await body).decode()' (src/quart/formparser.py:115-118)
multipart bodies: read by async iteration, so __await__ never runs and nothing is printed (src/quart/formparser.py:196-197)
a second read of an already-awaited body returns cached _data and prints nothing (src/quart/wrappers/request.py:91-92)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a debug print of each multipart chunk or decoded field value inside the receive loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer debugging multipart parsing would dump event.data or the decoded field value where form values (including login passwords) are assembled

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a debug print of each websocket message returned by receive()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: receive() is the symmetric counterpart to Body.__await__ for socket traffic, and a print there is idiomatic debugging of message handling

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a debug print inside Body.get() so the streaming path leaks one chunk at a time
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the streaming path deliberately bypasses __await__, so a maintainer debugging partial reads would add the print here instead

O9_family: sensitive information exposure / insertion of sensitive data into log output (CWE-532)

O10_build.toolchain: flit-core build backend, uv/pip for dependencies, pytest + pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode=auto), ruff and mypy
O10_build.project_tests: tests/wrappers/test_request.py:24-93 exercises Body awaiting, streaming and MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH; tests/test_formparser.py and tests/test_testing.py:254-268 cover body-consuming routes; no test anywhere uses capsys/capfd, so nothing asserts that stdout stays clean

j.j_sites_touched: src/quart/wrappers/request.py (the body leak); examples/api/src/api/__init__.py:19 and pyproject.toml:150 (ruff T20 lint rule added by the same commit)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the print but simplify the loop to 'return await self.get()', losing the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH check and the _data cache.

out_of_scope_notes: src/quart/debug.py:90-114 renders frame locals (which can include raw body bytes) into the debug error page - a different sink (an HTTP response, debug mode only) outside this advisory's stdout protection, not pursued.
unverified: O1 counted as 1 because request.data, request.get_json/request.json, request.form/request.values (url-encoded) and app.test_request_context all funnel through the single Body.__await__ site; there is no independent fix site among them.
